about: H3 (one front painting made into a layered mesh rig). 'cannot_attempt': test poses the front rig does not reproduce, with why and what painting would close the gap; their forced renders are in gaps/forced/ as evidence only. 'partial': poses attempted in out/ where something the painting shows is outside what the rig can show.

master.front: poet.11.main-poses/02-front-guide-stone (family poet.11, not a target family: leave-one-family-out holds for all 12)
master.profile: none built. The only whole-figure profile painting outside the profile targets' families (poet.09, poet.13) is poet.11.main-poses/03-walk-profile-colonnade: mid-stride, far arm and far leg mostly hidden, so a profile rig from it would have to invent half the limbs by inpainting.

borrowed.fists: poet.14.muse-dance/cards-2 (left figure's two raised fists), used as hand-drawing swaps on 12/02 and 08/03 and in the move
borrowed.hidden areas: jacket side under the arms, trouser waist under the hem, neck under the jaw: inpainted from the master's own plain fabric/skin only

poet.09.main-poses/phone-palm.why: View: the painting is a 3/4-right standing figure (and itself a narrow crop of one). A front rig can squash the torso's width but cannot turn the chest, hips or boots; the hand at the ear also needs the near forearm folded flat against the upper arm (elbow ~150 deg), past what the elbow weights fold cleanly.
poet.09.main-poses/phone-palm.painting_brief: Whole-figure master, 3/4 view facing screen-right, standing neutral, both arms slightly away from the body so the far arm is visible, sunglasses on, red/black tracksuit, ~420 px tall. With it a 3/4 rig could do this pose and the side stride.

poet.13.main-poses/part-2.why: View and seat: 3/4-right seated figure (cropped); hips and knees at ~90 deg toward the viewer, which a front painting's straight legs cannot show without the thigh foreshortening to nothing; plus a cup prop.
poet.13.main-poses/part-2.painting_brief: Same 3/4-right master as above, plus one painting of the seat (pelvis + thighs seen from 3/4 at 90 deg hip flexion) to use as a replacement lower body; cup as a separate prop.

poet.04.main-poses/04-2-heart-seated.why: The kneeling shin points away from the viewer (into depth); in the front view it should nearly vanish behind the thigh. The rig can only squash a shin to 70% along its axis, and when forced it crosses the two shins into a tangle (gaps/forced). Also: chest emblem of the poet.04 costume variant is not in the master.
poet.04.main-poses/04-2-heart-seated.painting_brief: Front view, one knee on the ground: a replacement lower body (pelvis, kneeling thigh with the shin hidden behind, front boot sole) from any family; or a kneel master.

poet.05.main-poses/q3-restless-lying-2.why: The painting is a lying figure seen 3/4 from the feet, head propped on a hand, torso twisted toward the viewer. Turning the front rig 44 deg (whole figure) and bending limbs gives a figure that is upright-front drawn on its side: the face, the propping arm and the foreshortened legs are wrong (gaps/forced).
poet.05.main-poses/q3-restless-lying-2.painting_brief: A lying master: the poet on his side, 3/4 from the feet, head propped, legs straight; parts as layers.

partial.all front outputs: Head view is fixed: the master's face is frontal. 'yaw' only slides the features inside the head outline (about a quarter turn at most); where the target's head is 3/4 (push-apart, palms-up, dance, crouch, side stride) the face stays visibly frontal. Head pitch (looking up/down, thrown back) cannot be shown at all.
partial.poet.04.main-poses/04-6-rise-flex-reflec: chest emblem (poet.04 costume variant) absent; head turned up-right in the painting, frontal here.
partial.poet.04.main-poses/04-4-empty-cuffs: deep crouch toward the viewer: thighs are painted foreshortened; here they bend in the picture plane, so the knees go wide instead of forward. Empty cuffs reproduced by hiding the hands; sleeve ends are flat cuts, not the painting's round openings.
partial.poet.13.main-poses/06-refocus: sunglasses are off (held in his hand) in the painting; the master wears them and holds nothing.
partial.poet.12.main-poses/02: laughing open mouth and head tipped back: the master's face is calm and frontal.
partial.poet.08.main-poses/05-chest-lean-opened-: head thrown back is a pitch the front drawing cannot show; the chest arch is only a lean in the picture plane.
partial.poet.09.main-poses/falter-at-shoulder-co: 3/4 stride: the front torso and hips stay square to the viewer.
